Translate the predictions of a model into SQL

Source: R/predictSql.R
predictSql.Rd

Writes the prediction rule of a model fitted with fitMod as SQL code, so that the model can be scored directly in a database: as an UPDATE of a column, a SELECT, a CREATE TABLE ... AS or as bare expressions to paste into a query of one's own. The arguments output, type and s have the meaning and the defaults they have in predict.FitMod.

Usage

predictSql(
  object,
  table,
  output = c("prob", "class", "both", "where", "leaf"),
  s = "lambda.1se",
  type = NULL,
  statement = c("update", "select", "create", "expr"),
  into = NULL,
  id = NULL,
  target = NULL,
  vars = NULL,
  dialect = getOption("alloy.sqlDialect", "ansi"),
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'PredictSql'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

object

A fitted model of class "FitMod".

table

Name of the database table holding the predictors. Not needed for statement = "expr".

output

For classification models one of "prob" (default), "class" or "both"; for engine = "rpart" additionally "where" and "leaf". Ignored for regression and survival models.

s

For engine = "glmnet" only: the penalty parameter \(\lambda\), default "lambda.1se".

type

For regression models "response" (default) or "link"; for "coxph" "risk" (default) or "lp"; for the parametric survival models and "tobit" "response" (default) or "lp"; for "beta" also "precision" and "variance"; for "zeroinfl" "response" (default), "count" or "zero". For "logit" and "logitFirth" an explicit "link" or "response" yields a single column, as in predict.FitMod().

statement

The kind of SQL to write: "update" (default), "select", "create" or "expr", see Details.

into

Names of the columns the predictions are written to. If NULL (default) they are PRED for a single numeric prediction, P_<level> for class probabilities and PRED_CLASS for the predicted class.

id

The key of table, one or several column names. For "select" and "create" these columns are returned along with the predictions (if NULL, the default, all columns are). For "update" a key turns the statement into a MERGE that computes the linear predictor only once, see Details; with dialect = "exasol" this is the default even without a key (the rows are then identified by ROWID), and id = FALSE asks for the plain UPDATE.

target

For statement = "create": name of the new table.

vars

Named character vector mapping variable names of the model to column names of the database, e.g. c(Sepal.Length = "SEPAL_LENGTH"). Variables not listed keep their name. The column names are used as given (they may be quoted or qualified).

dialect

SQL dialect, one of "ansi", "exasol" or "mssql"; the default is taken from getOption("alloy.sqlDialect", "ansi"). "ansi" is understood by Oracle, PostgreSQL, Snowflake, DuckDB and most other databases. "exasol" guards the operations that abort a statement in Exasol, see Details. "mssql" is for Microsoft SQL Server (LOG() for the natural logarithm, SELECT ... INTO).

...

Not used.

x

An object of class "PredictSql".

Value

A character string of class "PredictSql" holding the statement, printed with cat(); for statement = "expr" a named character vector with one expression per output column. The attribute "exprs" always holds these expressions.

Details

Supported models. All models with a linear predictor: "lm", "lmrob", "logit", "logitFirth", "poisson", "quasipoisson", "gamma", "negbin", "beta", "tobit", "zeroinfl", "glmnet", "coxph", "weibull", "exponential", "lognormal", "loglogistic"; further "multinom", "polr" and "rpart". For the mixed models ("lmMixed", "logitMixed", ...) the population-level prediction is written, i.e. that of predict(object, re.form = NA); a message says so. The SQL reproduces predict.FitMod() up to floating point rounding.

Not supported are "nnet", "C5.0", "lda", "qda", "svm", "naiveBayes", "randomForest" and "xgboost"; further links without a closed form in SQL (probit), Cox models with strata, and terms that span several columns of the design matrix (poly(), ns(), bs(), matrices).

Terms. Within the formula the operators + - * / ^ and the functions log, log2, log10, log1p, exp, expm1, sqrt, abs and I() are translated, as are factor(), as.factor() and cut() with constant breaks. Interactions and any contrast coding are supported: the effect of each factor level (or combination of levels) is computed in R and written as one CASE expression. Anything else stops with an error rather than producing SQL that might be wrong. Factor levels are written as string literals; a numeric database column behind factor(x) relies on the implicit conversion of the database.

Missing values and unknown levels. A NULL in a predictor yields a NULL prediction (na.pass). So does a factor level that the model has not seen: it does not silently fall into the reference category. This holds for every predictor of the model, also for those whose coefficients are zero (aliased, or shrunk to zero by "glmnet"): they stay in the SQL with a coefficient of 0. For "rpart" there are no surrogate splits in SQL; a row whose split variable is NULL gets a NULL prediction, where predict() would use a surrogate.

Statements. "update" writes the predictions into existing columns of table; the columns must exist (the ALTER TABLE needed is in the attribute "ddl" of the result). "select" and "create" return the predictions along with id. "expr" returns the bare expressions as a named character vector.

Size of the SQL. Intermediate results - the linear predictor, the leaf of a tree - are needed several times: the inverse link refers to the linear predictor three times, a class probability of a multinomial model to all of them. Without id each reference is written out, and the statement grows accordingly. With id the intermediate results are computed once, in nested subqueries, and referred to by name. For "select" and "create" the subqueries are the statement itself; for "update" they are the source of a MERGE INTO table USING (...) ON (key), which requires id to identify the rows of table uniquely. So give id whenever the table has a key. In Exasol no key is needed: without id the MERGE joins on the pseudo column ROWID.

Exasol. A logarithm of a value that is not positive, a square root of a negative value or a division by zero is an error in Exasol and aborts the whole statement, where R returns -Inf, NaN or Inf for the row concerned. With dialect = "exasol" these operations are guarded (CASE WHEN x > 0 THEN LN(x) END, NULLIF(x, 0)) and yield NULL, so that a single such row costs its own prediction only. The ALTER TABLE statements use ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS and can be run repeatedly. Unquoted column names are folded to upper case by Exasol, so the variable names of the model need no mapping as long as the columns were created unquoted.

Coefficients are written with the 15 to 17 significant digits that reproduce the double exactly, in exponent notation, so that every database treats them as floating point numbers.

See also

predict.FitMod

Other modelling: classification-metrics, fitMod(), logitFirth, plot.FitMod(), predict.FitMod(), predictors(), print.FitMod(), regression-metrics

Examples

fitLogit <- fitMod(admit ~ gre + gpa + rank, Admit, engine = "logit")

# probability of the second class into an existing column
predictSql(fitLogit, table = "LAB.ADMIT", type = "response",
           into = "P_ADMIT")
#> UPDATE LAB.ADMIT
#> SET P_ADMIT =
#>   CASE WHEN (-3.9899790733310319e+00
#>   + 2.2644257861791518e-03 * gre
#>   + 8.0403754928022186e-01 * gpa
#>   + CASE
#>     WHEN rank = '1' THEN 0e+00
#>     WHEN rank = '2' THEN -6.7544292796356076e-01
#>     WHEN rank = '3' THEN -1.3402039164678872e+00
#>     WHEN rank = '4' THEN -1.5514636769180703e+00
#>   END) > 7e2 THEN 1e0 WHEN (-3.9899790733310319e+00
#>   + 2.2644257861791518e-03 * gre
#>   + 8.0403754928022186e-01 * gpa
#>   + CASE
#>     WHEN rank = '1' THEN 0e+00
#>     WHEN rank = '2' THEN -6.7544292796356076e-01
#>     WHEN rank = '3' THEN -1.3402039164678872e+00
#>     WHEN rank = '4' THEN -1.5514636769180703e+00
#>   END) < -7e2 THEN 0e0 ELSE 1e0 / (1e0 + EXP(-(-3.9899790733310319e+00
#>   + 2.2644257861791518e-03 * gre
#>   + 8.0403754928022186e-01 * gpa
#>   + CASE
#>     WHEN rank = '1' THEN 0e+00
#>     WHEN rank = '2' THEN -6.7544292796356076e-01
#>     WHEN rank = '3' THEN -1.3402039164678872e+00
#>     WHEN rank = '4' THEN -1.5514636769180703e+00
#>   END))) END;

# the same by key: a MERGE that computes the linear predictor once
predictSql(fitLogit, table = "LAB.ADMIT", type = "response",
           into = "P_ADMIT", id = "ID")
#> MERGE INTO LAB.ADMIT t
#> USING (
#>   SELECT ID,
#>     CASE WHEN ETA_ > 7e2 THEN 1e0 WHEN ETA_ < -7e2 THEN 0e0 ELSE 1e0 / (1e0 + EXP(-ETA_)) END AS P_ADMIT
#>   FROM (
#>     SELECT ID,
#>       -3.9899790733310319e+00
#>       + 2.2644257861791518e-03 * gre
#>       + 8.0403754928022186e-01 * gpa
#>       + CASE
#>         WHEN rank = '1' THEN 0e+00
#>         WHEN rank = '2' THEN -6.7544292796356076e-01
#>         WHEN rank = '3' THEN -1.3402039164678872e+00
#>         WHEN rank = '4' THEN -1.5514636769180703e+00
#>       END AS ETA_
#>     FROM LAB.ADMIT
#>   ) q1
#> ) q
#> ON (t.ID = q.ID)
#> WHEN MATCHED THEN UPDATE SET
#>   P_ADMIT = q.P_ADMIT;

# both class probabilities and the class, with the key
predictSql(fitLogit, table = "LAB.ADMIT", output = "both",
           statement = "select", id = "ID")
#> SELECT ID,
#>   (1e0 - P_) AS P_0,
#>   P_ AS P_1,
#>   CASE WHEN P_ > 5e-01 THEN '1' WHEN P_ <= 5e-01 THEN '0' END AS PRED_CLASS
#> FROM (
#>   SELECT ID,
#>     ETA_,
#>     CASE WHEN ETA_ > 7e2 THEN 1e0 WHEN ETA_ < -7e2 THEN 0e0 ELSE 1e0 / (1e0 + EXP(-ETA_)) END AS P_
#>   FROM (
#>     SELECT ID,
#>       -3.9899790733310319e+00
#>       + 2.2644257861791518e-03 * gre
#>       + 8.0403754928022186e-01 * gpa
#>       + CASE
#>         WHEN rank = '1' THEN 0e+00
#>         WHEN rank = '2' THEN -6.7544292796356076e-01
#>         WHEN rank = '3' THEN -1.3402039164678872e+00
#>         WHEN rank = '4' THEN -1.5514636769180703e+00
#>       END AS ETA_
#>     FROM LAB.ADMIT
#>   ) q1
#> ) q2;

# the linear predictor as a bare expression
predictSql(fitLogit, type = "link", statement = "expr")
#> -- PRED
#> -3.9899790733310319e+00
#>   + 2.2644257861791518e-03 * gre
#>   + 8.0403754928022186e-01 * gpa
#>   + CASE
#>     WHEN rank = '1' THEN 0e+00
#>     WHEN rank = '2' THEN -6.7544292796356076e-01
#>     WHEN rank = '3' THEN -1.3402039164678872e+00
#>     WHEN rank = '4' THEN -1.5514636769180703e+00
#>   END
